topic: Massage for swimmers' shoulders and lats

slides.headline: Laps adding up? Your lats know it
slides.sub: Where swimmers tend to tighten up and how massage can fit in.

slides.title: Where the load lands
slides.body: Every freestyle stroke pulls through the lats, chest and back of the shoulder. Thousands of strokes a week can leave these areas feeling tight and heavy.

slides.title: What massage can do
slides.body: Many swimmers find massage helps the shoulders and upper back feel looser and more relaxed. It's a nice complement to training, not a replacement for strength work.

slides.title: Timing around sessions
slides.body: A lighter massage a day or two before a hard set or race usually suits. Deeper work often sits better after a big week, with an easy swim the day after.

slides.title: Keep the gains between visits
slides.body: Use a foam roller on the lats for a minute each side, open your chest in a doorway, and keep up any band work your coach or physio has given you.

slides.title: When it's more than tightness
slides.body: Pain that catches mid-stroke, clicking with pain, or a shoulder that wakes you at night is worth a physio assessment. Our team can refer you across.

slides.headline: Shoulders feeling the kilometres?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work on your shoulders, lats and upper back to help you feel loose for your next set. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
All those laps add up, especially through your lats and shoulders. 🏊

Freestyle loads the lats, chest and back of the shoulder thousands of times a week. Many swimmers find remedial massage helps those areas feel looser and recover between sessions.

Keep expectations realistic: massage complements strength work and good technique rather than replacing them. A lighter session suits before a hard set, deeper work after a big week. Pain that catches mid-stroke or wakes you at night is worth a physio check.
